data.one_liner: Authenticate users with web services and OAuth2 via native web authentication sessions.
data.what_it_does: A Flutter plugin that opens a web browser view to authenticate users with third-party web services or OAuth2 providers and handles custom scheme redirects back to the app. It uses ASWebAuthenticationSession on iOS/macOS and Chrome Custom Tabs on Android.
use_when: You need to implement OAuth2 authentication flows in your Flutter app.
You want to authenticate users using external web services via custom URL schemes.
avoid_when: You are looking for built-in Firebase Authentication flows.
You only want standard Google Sign-In helper packages without manual OAuth HTTP token exchanges.
strengths: Uses native platform authentication sessions (ASWebAuthenticationSession and Chrome Custom Tabs)
Supports iOS, Android, macOS, and Web platforms
Works well with standard OAuth2 providers
weaknesses: Requires manual configuration of intent filters on Android and custom HTML landing pages on Web
Known minor issues with keyboard accessibility or Chrome default browser bugs on macOS
data.setup_notes: Requires adding a custom CallbackActivity intent filter in AndroidManifest.xml and setting up a callback HTML file for web platforms.

alternatives.name: google_sign_in
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you specifically need a dedicated, out-of-the-box wrapper for Google Sign-In instead of a generic web auth flow.

alternatives.name: firebase_auth
alternatives.why_pick_it: If your backend is Firebase and you prefer using their integrated authentication suite.

alternatives.name: sign_in_with_apple
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you specifically need dedicated Sign in with Apple integration.
